questions_and_answers.question: What does the use of ‘पड़’ after an infinitive indicate?

answers.answer: An inescapable necessity or strong obligation

articles.text:
The use of ‘पड़’ after an infinitive expresses inescapable necessity or the strongest kind of obligation. It is used in all tenses and suggests some kind of external force. Example sentences include:

• मुझे डॉक्टर के पास जाना पड़ता है — I must go to see the doctor.
• उसे दवा खानी पड़ती थी — She used to have to take medicine.
• हमें टीके लगवाने पड़ेंगे — We’ll have to take our shots.
• उसका इंतज़ार करना पड़ा — (Somebody) had to wait for him.
• बहुत किस्म की मशीनों के प्रयोग करने पड़े — It was necessary to use all kinds of machines.

Adding the clarifier ‘जाना’ after a verb root sometimes suggests that the action is carried out completely. For example:
• पी जाइये — Bottoms up!
• मैं खा गई — I ate it all up.
However, in many cases the clarifier contributes very little to the meaning, and forms without the clarifier (except with न or नहीं) are also acceptable, such as समझें? versus समझ गये? and मरे versus मर गये. A clarifier adds only a shade of meaning and has little relationship to its meaning as a main verb.
